content.comment_body: Hello, I purchased two software products for [product_name] PLCs. The first software was [product_name] [product_name] v3.0 provided on 4 floppy disks, and the second was [product_name] [product_name] Comfort v7.0 supplied on CD. My PC had a more recent version of [product_name] [product_name] Comfort v8.4.0, but I discovered a newer version was available and downloaded it. After the installation, I could no longer detect the USB ports needed to connect to older-generation PLCs. Upon uninstalling the updated [product_name], both software versions appeared to be active in the PC’s uninstall program. Removing the new version also deleted the previous one. Now, when I attempt to install [product_name] [product_name] Comfort v7.0 from the CD, I encounter an error that prevents installation. Please advise on how to restore the software. Thank you in advance, best regards [user_name].
Hello [user_name], English is preferred in this forum. Please write your posts in English. Thank you.

Uninstall all versions and delete all related directories. Download the newest upgrade version, which supports previous hardware including USB. The selection for USB might be located differently within the software. Insert your purchased v7 CD (not the demo version) without installing it. Proceed with the installation of the downloaded version as an upgrade. When prompted for the path to the old version, select the CD—possibly a specific subdirectory—so the software recognizes your valid license. You can then complete installation on your PC without issue.

analysis.insight_summary: After updating [product_name] [product_name] Comfort, the user experienced loss of USB connectivity for older PLC hardware. The uninstall process removed both new and previous software versions, leaving the user unable to reinstall the licensed older version due to errors. This interruption affected workflow and created uncertainty around software licensing and installation steps.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to upgrade and revert between software versions without losing access or functionality, especially for connecting legacy PLCs, and desires clear instructions to avoid license or installation issues.
